Create a Mona webpage with Copilot CLI

From a terminal prompt to a generated webpage and a connected web session.

9documented steps
9evidence screenshots
2:55source recording
Prototype, not an approved SOP. Selected video frames; visible actions and on-screen text only. Audio has not been transcribed. This SOP documents the recorded demo, not a verified product-support statement. Timestamps identify sampled evidence, not exact action boundaries.

Purpose

Create a local animated HTML page using GitHub Copilot CLI, then access the same agent conversation through GitHub's web interface.

Source: demo-ghc-cli.mp4

Prerequisites

  • A Windows computer with GitHub Copilot CLI installed and authenticated. Installation and sign-in are not shown in the recording.
  • An approved local working folder where generating an HTML file is permitted.
  • A web browser and a GitHub account with the necessary Copilot access.
  • Permission to use remote session access under your organization's policies.

Safety & limitations

  • The recording enables all tool permissions and uses the user's home folder. Do not treat these demo choices as recommended practice: use a dedicated folder and least-privilege approvals.
  • Inspect generated HTML before opening it. Generated code and assistant claims require human verification.
  • Screenshots contain account and desktop context. Review and redact them before sharing outside the approved audience.
  • The final animation and mobile-access behavior have not been exhaustively tested. No process-owner approval is recorded.
01
STEP 1 / 9

Confirm the working folder

0:04

Action

Start Copilot CLI in your approved working folder. Review the displayed path and confirm trust only if you recognize and trust the folder.

Expected outcome

The interactive Copilot CLI prompt becomes available.

Review note

The recording starts with Copilot already open; the exact launch command is not visible. Avoid trusting an unnecessarily broad folder.

Evidence: Observed prompt

02
STEP 2 / 9

Request the animated webpage

0:33

Action

Enter the request below and allow Copilot to generate the HTML file, reviewing any requested permissions.

create a static HTML web page, displaying an fun animation of Mona

Expected outcome

Copilot begins creating a static page featuring Mona, GitHub's Octocat.

Evidence: Observed request

03
STEP 3 / 9

Review the generated result

1:03

Action

Check that mona-animation.html has been created. Review the generated code and the assistant's description before opening the file.

Expected outcome

The assistant lists floating motion, blinking eyes, animated tentacles, stars, bubbles, and click effects.

Review note

This screenshot establishes what Copilot reported, not that every animation or interaction works correctly.

Evidence: Assistant-reported result

04
STEP 4 / 9

Open the HTML page

1:17

Action

Ask Copilot to open the generated file using the command below. If Windows asks which application to use, choose an approved browser.

start mona-animation.html

Expected outcome

The local HTML file opens in the selected browser.

Review note

Choosing a browser once is sufficient; changing the system default is not required.

Evidence: Observed application chooser

05
STEP 5 / 9

Enable remote session access

1:52

Action

If remote access is allowed by your organization, return to the CLI and run /remote on.

/remote on

Expected outcome

Copilot establishes a remote connection and displays a session link.

Review note

This is an optional connectivity step, not a prerequisite for generating the local HTML page.

Evidence: Observed command selection

06
STEP 6 / 9

Open the connected session link

1:57

Action

Open the GitHub session URL provided by your own CLI session. Authenticate if required by your organization.

Expected outcome

GitHub opens the conversation associated with the running CLI session.

Review note

Use your own generated URL, not the personal session address visible in this recording.

Evidence: Observed connection confirmation

07
STEP 7 / 9

Check conversation continuity on the web

2:01

Action

Confirm that the web conversation contains the CLI request and response. Look for the remote-mode indicator before continuing the conversation.

Expected outcome

The CLI conversation is visible in the GitHub web interface, with remote mode enabled.

Evidence: Observed web session

08
STEP 8 / 9

Inspect the generated webpage

2:45

Action

Switch to the local webpage tab and inspect the displayed result. Check animation and click effects manually before accepting the output.

Expected outcome

The generated page displays Mona on a dark background with stars.

Review note

The screenshot confirms the visible design, but cannot prove animation timing or successful click behavior.

Evidence: Observed page

09
STEP 9 / 9

Continue the conversation

2:54

Action

Use the web conversation for follow-up questions. The recording asks whether the session can also be accessed through GitHub Mobile.

Expected outcome

The web interface displays the submitted question and an assistant response.

Review note

Mobile access is described by the assistant but not demonstrated. Validate supported versions and policies separately; do not mark mobile access as tested.

Evidence: Observed web exchange; mobile claim unverified
